subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Graphs of functions

points.text: Sketching from given information or a context; copying a GDC graph onto paper
Graphing functions, including sums and differences, with technology

bigPicture: A good sketch communicates shape and key points, not exact scale. Paper 2 expects her to transfer a GDC graph to paper with the right features labelled.

keyIdeas.answer: Correct shape, intercepts, turning points, asymptotes (dashed) and the domain endpoints, labelled with coordinates.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you graph f + g with technology?
keyIdeas.answer: Enter both, or enter y = f(x) + g(x) directly; use a sensible window.

keyTerms.def: shows shape and key features; not to scale

misconceptions.right: It needs labelled features, not a scale.
Respect the given domain; adjust the window.

practice.prompt: Sketch y = (x − 1)(x + 3) showing intercepts and vertex.
Sketch y = 2^x − x² for −2 ≤ x ≤ 5, labelling all x-intercepts.
commonErrors: Missing the negative root because of the window

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: Which key features (2.4) should every sketch label?
